items.title: Rieffel's theorem on the bicommutant of a right ideal
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file brauer.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states Rieffel's theorem: for a ring with no nontrivial two-sided ideal and a nonzero right ideal, the ring coincides with the bicommutant of that right ideal (statement lines 308-314). The proof is a complete argument: the natural map from the ring to the bicommutant is shown injective using the absence of nontrivial two-sided ideals (proof lines 316-324); the image of the ideal is shown to be a right ideal in the bicommutant because left multiplication by an element of the ideal is an endomorphism of the module (proof lines 324-330); and since the product ideal is two-sided and hence the whole ring, the image of the ring is a right ideal in the bicommutant containing the identity, which forces equality (proof lines 330-333). The non-formal content is the definition of the module structure on the far side and the two-sidedness argument. The claim is H2.
